name: Herringbone jacket

lead: A herringbone jacket is cut from cloth woven in a broken-twill zigzag that resembles the skeleton of a herring. It is usually wool and is often tweed, a combination used for sport coats, blazers and outerwear.
In style circles the appeal is visual: the pattern gives a jacket subtle texture and a classic, structured look without a loud print.

paras: It is worn as a sport coat or blazer over shirts and knitwear, or as outerwear in heavier tweeds. Grey, brown and charcoal herringbones are common in tweed, according to general menswear convention.
No health risks beyond wool allergy or irritation for sensitive wearers. Fit and tailoring matter more than the pattern for how the jacket looks.

chain: Visible depth without a bold print
angle.text: The pattern adds subtle surface texture, so a plain outfit looks more considered. A well-fitted jacket in any cloth also shapes the shoulder and torso line.

lead: A herringbone jacket is a jacket made from herringbone cloth, a V-shaped broken twill weave usually made of wool [1]. The name comes from the pattern's resemblance to the skeleton of a herring fish [1].

Tweed is often woven in herringbone, with Donegal tweed a well-known example [1]. Tweed has long been tied to country wear such as shooting jackets and was later adopted more widely; typical tweed sport coats use patterns such as herringbone, houndstooth and glen plaid [2].
People wear herringbone jackets to add texture and a classic, structured look to an outfit. No clinical studies exist on the garment.

paras: Herringbone, also called broken twill weave, differs from a plain chevron because the direction breaks at each reversal [1]. It is one of the most popular fabrics for suits and outerwear [1]. Harris Tweed is defined in law as handwoven in the Outer Hebrides from pure virgin wool [2].

Herringbone weaves appear in antiquity, including Alpine woollen leggings from 800 to 500 BC and a textile from Pompeii [1]. Tweed was originally called "tweel", Scots for twill, and became linked to upper-class country wear before spreading to the Edwardian middle classes [2]. Durability and moisture resistance suited it to outdoor pursuits [2].

Menswear commentary commonly pairs a herringbone jacket with plain shirts and trousers so the texture reads without competing patterns. Grey Donegal tweed sport coats are a typical example of the form [2].

timeline.event: Herringbone woollen leggings from the Alps [1].
Harris Tweed Act defines the cloth [2].
